steps.title: Import TypeScript types and sessionStorage API
steps.instruction: Import the necessary TypeScript types and reference the sessionStorage API. Since this is a TypeScript-only lesson, you'll need to import the appropriate types and reference the browser's sessionStorage API.
steps.hint: You'll need to import the 'Storage' type from the TypeScript DOM library and reference the global sessionStorage object.
steps.seedCode: // Import the necessary types and reference sessionStorage
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the required imports and sessionStorage reference to build the typed wrapper.
successCriteria: The Storage type is imported from the appropriate TypeScript DOM library, and sessionStorage is referenced from the global window object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Storage type and referenced sessionStorage. This gives us the foundation to build our typed wrapper.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing the Storage type and referencing sessionStorage from the global window object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. For this step, you need to import the Storage type and reference the sessionStorage API.

steps.title: Define the generic StorageWrapper interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named StorageWrapper with three generic methods: get, set, and remove.
steps.hint: Use the interface keyword followed by StorageWrapper. Inside, declare methods with appropriate signatures using a generic type parameter T.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the necessary types and reference sessionStorage

// Define the StorageWrapper interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a typed interface that defines the contract for storage operations with proper TypeScript generics.
successCriteria: StorageWrapper interface is defined with get, set, and remove methods using a generic type parameter T.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the StorageWrapper interface with proper generic typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure all three methods (get, set, remove) are defined with correct signatures using the generic type T.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the interface keyword and include all three methods with proper TypeScript syntax.

steps.title: Create the typedSessionStorage function signature
steps.instruction: Declare a function named typedSessionStorage that returns an object implementing the StorageWrapper interface. Use a generic type parameter <T> to make it type-safe.
steps.hint: Start with 'function typedSessionStorage<T>(): StorageWrapper<T> { }' or use an arrow function with the same signature.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function signature for typedSessionStorage is added, ready to implement the wrapper methods.
successCriteria: The typedSessionStorage function is declared with a generic type parameter <T> and returns StorageWrapper<T>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the typedSessionStorage function signature correctly with proper TypeScript generics.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function returns StorageWrapper<T> and uses a generic type parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function signature is missing or incorrect. It should accept a generic type and return StorageWrapper<T>.

steps.title: Implement the get method with type safety
steps.instruction: Inside the typedSessionStorage function, implement the get method that retrieves a value from sessionStorage, parses it as JSON, and returns typed data.
steps.hint: The get method should take a key parameter, use sessionStorage.getItem(key), parse the result with JSON.parse, and return it with the appropriate type.
steps.expectedOutcome: The typedSessionStorage function now has a get method that retrieves and parses sessionStorage items with type safety.
successCriteria: The get method is implemented, uses sessionStorage.getItem, parses JSON, and returns typed data or null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented a type-safe get method that properly handles sessionStorage retrieval and JSON parsing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your get method retrieves from sessionStorage, parses the JSON, and returns the typed value or null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The get method isn't implemented correctly. It should retrieve from sessionStorage, parse JSON, and return typed data.

steps.title: Implement the set method with JSON serialization
steps.instruction: Inside the typedSessionStorage function, implement the set method on the returned object. The method should accept a key (string) and a value of type T, then store it in sessionStorage using JSON.stringify.
steps.hint: Add a set method to the object returned by typedSessionStorage. Use sessionStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value)).
steps.expectedOutcome: The typedSessionStorage function returns an object with both get and set methods. The set method serializes the value to JSON and stores it in sessionStorage.
successCriteria: The set method is implemented with correct parameters (key: string, value: T) and stores the value using sessionStorage.setItem and JSON.stringify.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the set method with type-safe JSON serialization.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the set method accepts a key and a value, and uses JSON.stringify before storing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The set method is missing or incorrect. It should store the value in sessionStorage after converting it to a JSON string.

steps.title: Implement the remove method
steps.instruction: Inside the typedSessionStorage function, implement the remove method that calls sessionStorage.removeItem(key) to delete an item from storage.
steps.hint: Add a remove method to the returned object that takes a key parameter and removes the item from sessionStorage.
steps.expectedOutcome: The typedSessionStorage function now returns an object with a remove method that removes items from sessionStorage.
successCriteria: The remove method is implemented with the correct signature and calls sessionStorage.removeItem.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the remove method to delete items from sessionStorage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the remove method takes a key parameter and calls sessionStorage.removeItem(key).
steps.feedbackWrong: The remove method is not implemented correctly. Check the method signature and ensure it calls sessionStorage.removeItem.

steps.title: Return the wrapper object with all methods
steps.instruction: Complete the typedSessionStorage function by returning an object that contains the get, set, and remove methods you implemented.
steps.hint: The function should return an object with three methods: get, set, and remove. Make sure each method is properly defined with its parameters and return type.
steps.expectedOutcome: The typedSessionStorage function now returns a complete wrapper object with all three methods defined.
successCriteria: The typedSessionStorage function returns an object containing get, set, and remove methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the wrapper object with all required methods.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the returned object includes all three methods: get, set, and remove.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't return a complete wrapper object. Check that you're returning an object with get, set, and remove methods.

steps.title: Create a usage example with a specific type
steps.instruction: Define a User interface with name and age properties, then create a typed wrapper instance for it.
steps.hint: Create an interface with name: string and age: number, then call typedSessionStorage<User>() to get a typed wrapper.
steps.expectedOutcome: A User interface and a typed wrapper instance created for demonstration.
successCriteria: User interface is defined with name:string and age:number
typedSessionStorage<User>() is called to create a wrapper instance
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a concrete type and created a typed wrapper instance for it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined the User interface with both properties and called typedSessionStorage<User>().
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined the User interface and created a typed wrapper instance using typedSessionStorage<User>().

steps.title: Test the wrapper by storing and retrieving typed data
steps.instruction: In the usage example area, call the wrapper's set method to store a User object, then call get to retrieve it and log the result to the console.
steps.hint: After creating your wrapper instance, use wrapper.set('userKey', userObject) to store data, then const retrieved = wrapper.get('userKey') to retrieve it. Finally, console.log('Retrieved user:', retrieved).
steps.expectedOutcome: The wrapper will successfully store a typed User object in sessionStorage and retrieve it with proper type safety, demonstrating the wrapper's functionality.
successCriteria: The wrapper's set method is called with a User object, the get method retrieves it, and the result is logged to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested the typed wrapper by storing and retrieving typed data. The console log confirms the wrapper works correctly with type safety.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling both set and get methods on your wrapper instance and logging the retrieved result to the console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The testing code doesn't seem to be complete. Remember to call wrapper.set() with a User object, then wrapper.get() to retrieve it, and finally console.log() the result.

steps.title: Add error handling for JSON parsing
steps.instruction: In the get method of your typedSessionStorage function, wrap the JSON.parse call in a try-catch block to handle parsing errors gracefully.
steps.hint: Add try { ... } catch { ... } around the parsing logic. In the catch block, return null to indicate the data couldn't be retrieved.
steps.expectedOutcome: The get method will now safely handle invalid JSON data by returning null instead of throwing an error.
successCriteria: The get method contains a try-catch block that wraps JSON.parse and returns null in the catch block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've made the wrapper robust by adding error handling for JSON parsing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the try-catch block is properly implemented in the get method.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a try-catch block around the JSON.parse call in the get method to handle parsing errors.
